title: dedicated-autoscaler: improve burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Improve dedicated autoscaler stability: tighten burst controls, add throughput guarantee enforcement, and extend utilization telemetry. Backwards-compatible config additions. Recommended for next minor release.
description: Motivation: Dedicated customers occasionally saw short-lived traffic spikes that exhausted reserved capacity and degraded tail latency. The autoscaler allowed large token bursts which increased eviction and rebalancing churn. This PR tightens burst controls, adds a configurable throughput guarantee path to prioritize reserved capacity, and enhances utilization reporting so SREs can reason about burst consumption vs baseline throughput. Summary of changes: 1) New config knobs: autoscaler.burst_window_ms (default 60000), autoscaler.burst_tokens (default 2000), autoscaler.burst_penalty_ms (default 300000). 2) Introduced throughput_guarantee policy: capacity_reservation_pct and min_steady_rps settings that can be used to reserve a fraction of fleet capacity for steady traffic. 3) Telemetry: new metrics dedicated.autoscaler.burst_used_tokens, dedicated.autoscaler.burst_penalty_active, dedicated.fleet.throughput_guarantee_util, and dedicated.node.idle_cycles. 4) Reporting: added a daily utilization rollup that separates baseline vs burst consumption and surfaces top-10 bursty routes. 5) Safety: added fallback to compatible model variants when throughput_guarantee cannot be met. 6) Tests and docs: unit+integration tests for burst windowing logic, load test harness extension, and console docs. Implementation notes: The autoscaler now maintains a per-fleet sliding window counter for burst tokens instead of purely queue-length heuristics. We compute burst allowance as min(burst_tokens_remaining, token_budget_for_request) and apply a penalty period when allowance is exceeded to avoid repeated short bursts. The throughput guarantee path tags requests with reservation_id and routes them through reserved pools when capacity_reservation_pct is >0. Small config example: autoscaler: { burst_window_ms: 60000, burst_tokens: 2000, burst_penalty_ms: 300000, throughput_guarantee: { capacity_reservation_pct: 20, min_steady_rps: 50 } } Note: config keys are additive and default to previous behavior when unset. Backwards compatible unless users opt into throughput_guarantee.
commits_summary: a) Add burst window token bucket and penalty logic (autoscaler/*) b) Implement throughput_guarantee routing and reservation bookkeeping (router/*) c) Add new telemetry and rollup jobs (observability/*) d) Integration tests and load harness updates (perf-canary/) e) Docs + console UX copy (redwood-docs/console) f) Minor refactors and lint fixes
review_comments: Evan: Can we add a unit test that simulates interleaved small and large requests to exercise the penalty window? currently the integration test covers steady bursts but not interleaving.
Priya: Added an interleaving unit test in autoscaler/burst_window_test.go; it failed initially due to clock granularity, fixed by introducing a mockable monotonic clock.
Liam: Nit: variable names in burst_window.go could be clearer (remainingTokens -> tokensRemaining). Not blocking.
Maya: How does this interact with per-customer quotas? Is there a risk reserved capacity is starved? Please document and add an e2e scenario.

Priya: Documented interaction in redwood-docs and added an e2e in perf-canary to validate per-customer quotas are respected when throughput_guarantee is enabled. Also added a safety check to avoid double-reserving the same request.
merge_outcome: Merged to main after approval from Evan and Maya. All CI green. Deployed to staging for soak and rolled to prod with a graduated rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Notify customers with reserved capacity via email template about throughput_guarantee opt-in (PM-1192)
